sentences.en: If you've ever driven into New York City from the north, there's a good chance you've passed by a massive cluster of high-rise apartment buildings just as you enter the Bronx.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾开车从北边进入纽约市，很有可能在刚进入布朗克斯区时，经过过一大片高层公寓楼群。

sentences.en: 35 buildings in total, all of them with identical brick facades, all over 20 stories tall.
sentences.zh: 总共35栋楼，外墙砖面一模一样，全都超过20层高。

sentences.en: I remember the first time I saw these buildings, riding a Greyhound bus into the city from Worcester, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 我记得第一次见到这些建筑时，我正坐着灰狗巴士从马萨诸塞州的伍斯特市进城。

sentences.en: 99PI producer Emeritus Katie Mingle is back to tell our story this week.
sentences.zh: 本周由《99%隐形》荣誉制作人凯蒂·明格尔回来为我们讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: I was in my early 20s at the time, and I'd never really seen skyscrapers that weren't office buildings.
sentences.zh: 那时我才20出头，此前从未见过非办公楼的摩天大楼。

sentences.en: These buildings, I could tell, were people's homes.
sentences.zh: 我看得出来，这些建筑是人们的家。

sentences.en: I could see laundry hanging on balconies way up on, like, the 22nd floor.
sentences.zh: 我能看到晾衣架挂在22层那么高的阳台上。

sentences.en: There was something thrilling, but also almost frightening, about contemplating the number of individual lives playing out in just one of those skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 想到仅仅在那一栋摩天大楼里，就有那么多鲜活的生命在演绎着各自的人生，这既让人兴奋，又几乎让人感到恐惧。

sentences.en: It had the effect of making me feel very small and insignificant.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到自己非常渺小和微不足道。

sentences.en: The way looking at something incomprehensibly large can sometimes do.
sentences.zh: 就像面对某种无法理解的庞然大物时，人有时会有的那种感觉。

sentences.en: I think I assumed at the time that what I was looking at was a public housing project.
sentences.zh: 我想当时我以为自己看到的是公共住房项目。

sentences.en: But I know now that it wasn't.
This cluster of high-rises was, and is, the largest housing cooperative in the world.
sentences.zh: 这片高层建筑群过去是，现在依然是世界上最大的住房合作社。

sentences.en: When Co-op City opened in the late 1960s, people hated the way it looked.
sentences.zh: 当合作城在20世纪60年代末落成时，人们非常讨厌它的外观。

sentences.en: Journalists and architecture critics thought the buildings embodied everything that was wrong with modernist architecture.
sentences.zh: 记者和建筑评论家认为这些建筑体现了现代主义建筑的所有弊病。

sentences.en: The towers of New York City's Co-op City rise bleak and spectrally through the smog, a prospect so remote and cheerless that affluent commuters often shudder when they pass it.
sentences.zh: 纽约合作城的塔楼在雾霾中显得阴郁而幽灵般，这景象如此遥远且毫无生气，以至于富裕的通勤者经过时常会不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Those comments are exactly why Co-op City is the best-kept secret, because it's like hiding in plain sight.
sentences.zh: 这些评论恰恰说明了为什么合作城是“隐藏在眼皮底下的秘密”，因为它就像是藏在显眼处。

sentences.en: You look at the exterior, you make your judgment, and you just keep moving, and you don't give it another thought.
sentences.zh: 你看着它的外观，做出你的判断，然后继续赶路，再也不会去想它。

sentences.en: Diane moved into her Co-op City apartment in 1978.
sentences.zh: 黛安在1978年搬进了她在合作城的公寓。

sentences.en: I think I paid $2,500 for the apartment.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时为这套公寓付了2500美元。

sentences.en: Diane doesn't pay rent, but she doesn't exactly own the unit either.
sentences.zh: 黛安不付租金，但她也不完全拥有这套单元。

sentences.en: Technically, when she handed over that $2,500, she was buying a share in a corporation.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，当她交出那2500美元时，她购买的是一家公司的股份。
这就是合作社的运作方式。

sentences.en: The housing development itself is a corporation, and when you buy a share, you are buying the right to live in a specific unit.
sentences.zh: 住房开发项目本身就是一家公司，当你购买股份时，你购买的是居住在特定单元的权利。

sentences.en: Together, all the residents of a cooperative collectively own the corporation that is their building.
sentences.zh: 合作社的所有居民共同拥有他们所在的建筑公司。

sentences.en: Do you feel like you're an owner?
Yes, we can do things inside our unit, whatever we want.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们可以在自己的单元内做任何想做的事。

sentences.en: We do our own painting and flooring and whatever improvements we want to do.
sentences.zh: 我们可以自己粉刷、铺地板，做任何我们想做的改进。

sentences.en: On top of that initial $2,500 investment, every month Diane pays what are called carrying charges.
sentences.zh: 除了最初的2500美元投资，黛安每个月还要支付所谓的“运营费”。

sentences.en: For Diane, these are about $800 a month, and they cover the mortgage and utilities like heat, electricity, and air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 对黛安来说，这大约是每月800美元，涵盖了抵押贷款和供暖、电力、空调等公用事业费用。

sentences.en: Like, what does it look like?
I think it's like 850 square feet.
sentences.zh: 我想大约有850平方英尺（约79平方米）。

sentences.en: And it's large, and it's beautiful.
Diane used to work in real estate, so she's particularly aware of how lucky she is to have a place she likes at a price she can afford.
sentences.zh: 黛安以前从事房地产工作，所以她特别清楚能以负担得起的价格拥有自己喜欢的房子是多么幸运。

sentences.en: I saw what people were paying for tiny, teeny, teeny little apartments in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 我见过人们为曼哈顿那些极小、极小、极小的公寓付出了多少钱。

sentences.en: You know, you'd have to have a big pile of money, endless money, because they're not made for people who are just ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你得有一大笔钱，花不完的钱，因为那些房子不是为普通人准备的。

sentences.en: I know what Diane is getting at here.
In major cities like New York, sometimes it feels like there's public housing for low-income families and market-rate housing that is insanely expensive, with not much in-between.
sentences.zh: 在纽约这样的大城市，有时感觉只有为低收入家庭提供的公共住房，和贵得离谱的市场价住房，中间几乎没有过渡。

sentences.en: Co-op City, though, is that in-between in a couple of different ways.
sentences.zh: 然而，合作城在几个方面恰恰就是那种过渡。

sentences.en: It's in-between renting and owning, and it offers some of the perks of both.
sentences.zh: 它介于租房和买房之间，并提供两者的部分好处。

sentences.en: It's also in-between in terms of coSt.
sentences.zh: 它在成本上也处于中间地带。

sentences.en: Co-op City was specifically intended to be affordable for middle-class New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 合作城专门旨在为中产阶级纽约人提供负担得起的住房。

sentences.en: In fact, it was part of a whole movement to build this kind of in-between middle-class housing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它是建设这种中间地带中产阶级住房运动的一部分。

sentences.en: Co-op City was the crowning achievement of that movement.
sentences.zh: 合作城是那场运动的最高成就。

sentences.en: And also, the end of it.
This story begins with a Russian immigrant named Abraham Kazin.
sentences.zh: 这个故事始于一位名叫亚伯拉罕·卡津的俄罗斯移民。

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, Kazin was a young socialist and a union organizer.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初，卡津是一位年轻的社会主义者和工会组织者。

sentences.en: But what he was really passionate about actually went beyond the normal work of unions.
sentences.zh: 但他真正热衷的事情实际上超出了工会的常规工作。

sentences.en: He was very interested in cooperatives.
sentences.zh: 他对合作社非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: He's a historian who's written about labor and housing.
sentences.zh: 他是一位研究劳工和住房的历史学家。

sentences.en: This was a viable alternative to capitalism, to market systems, that you could sort of develop within an existing capitalist society.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可行的替代资本主义和市场体系的选择，你可以在现有的资本主义社会内部发展出这种模式。

sentences.en: Kazin pursued a few different cooperative ventures before turning his attention to the thing that would become his life's work, housing.
sentences.zh: 卡津在将注意力转向他毕生的事业——住房之前，曾尝试过几种不同的合作社项目。

sentences.en: At this point, he's an organizer for the Amalgamated Clothing Workers Union of America, which represented garment workers.
sentences.zh: 此时，他是美国联合服装工人工会的组织者，该工会代表服装工人。

sentences.en: These garment workers were mostly living on the Lower East Side in these cramped, unhealthy, run-down slum tenements.
sentences.zh: 这些服装工人大多住在下东区的那些狭窄、不卫生、破旧的贫民窟公寓里。

sentences.en: By 1920 or so, Kazin was convinced that the union should help get rid of the predatory landlords who owned these tenements.
sentences.zh: 到1920年左右，卡津确信工会应该帮助摆脱那些拥有这些公寓的掠夺性房东。

sentences.en: He thought that the union should construct its own apartment buildings and let its members become collective owners.
sentences.zh: 他认为工会应该建造自己的公寓楼，让成员成为集体业主。

sentences.en: And it was actually a concept that New Yorkers already understood.
sentences.zh: 而且这实际上是一个纽约人已经理解的概念。

sentences.en: The origins of co-ops don't come from the working or radical milieu.
sentences.zh: 合作社的起源并非来自工人阶级或激进派。

sentences.en: This was something that rich people came up with.
sentences.zh: 这是富人想出来的东西。

sentences.en: You know, I'm sitting in a co-op building right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我现在就坐在一栋合作社大楼里。

sentences.en: I live in a building with about 100 apartments.
sentences.zh: 我住的楼里大约有100套公寓。

sentences.en: And the 100 of us residents, we collectively own this building.
sentences.zh: 我们100位居民共同拥有这栋楼。

sentences.en: But it's a middle-class, an upper-middle-class building.
sentences.zh: 但这是一栋中产阶级、中上层阶级的建筑。

sentences.en: And if someone moves out, they sell their apartment.
sentences.zh: 如果有人搬走，他们就会卖掉他们的公寓。

sentences.en: What they think of is selling their apartment, they're really selling the shares in the corporation, you know, on the open market.
sentences.zh: 他们所想的卖掉公寓，实际上是在公开市场上出售公司的股份，你懂的。

sentences.en: And if they sell it for more than they bought it, more power to them.
sentences.zh: 如果他们卖出的价格比买入时高，那是他们的本事。

sentences.en: They have to keep the money.
But that's not how Kazin envisioned his co-ops working.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是卡津设想的合作社运作方式。

sentences.en: In the kind of co-ops he wanted to build, when people moved out and sold their share in the corporation,
sentences.zh: 在他想要建立的那种合作社里，当人们搬走并出售公司股份时，

sentences.en: they'd get back the money they'd put in, but they wouldn't make a profit.
sentences.zh: 他们会拿回投入的钱，但不会赚取利润。

sentences.en: Removing profit would ensure the building stayed affordable into the future.
sentences.zh: 消除利润将确保建筑在未来保持可负担性。

sentences.en: But Kazin said at first, the Union Brass wasn't all that interested in his cooperative housing idea.
sentences.zh: 但卡津说，起初，工会高层对他的合作住房想法并不怎么感兴趣。

sentences.en: Here he is in an interview that he did late in his life.
sentences.zh: 这是他在晚年接受采访时说的话。

sentences.en: For a long while, I was the laughingstock in the organization when I spoke about building cooperative housing.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，当我谈论建设合作住房时，我是组织里的笑柄。

sentences.en: All my close friends used to make fun of me.
sentences.zh: 我所有的好朋友都取笑我。

sentences.en: Haters be damned by the late 1920s, Kazin and various union partners had built three new cooperative buildings
sentences.zh: 不管那些反对者怎么说，到20世纪20年代末，卡津和各工会合作伙伴已经建造了三栋新的合作社大楼，

sentences.en: that housed more than 850 working-class families.
sentences.zh: 安置了超过850个工人阶级家庭。

sentences.en: During the Great Depression and World War II, the work of building cooperative housing,
sentences.zh: 在大萧条和第二次世界大战期间，建设合作住房的工作，

sentences.en: or any housing for that matter, mostly just stopped.
sentences.zh: 或者说任何住房建设，基本上都停止了。

sentences.en: Which is why, after World War II, New York, along with a lot of urban America,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么二战后，纽约和许多美国城市一样，

sentences.en: found itself in a pretty acute housing shortage.
sentences.zh: 发现自己面临着相当严重的住房短缺。

sentences.en: In 1949, the federal government passed the American Housing Act to help fix it.
sentences.zh: 1949年，联邦政府通过了《美国住房法》来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: The new legislation had provisions to promote homeownership and the construction of public housing.
sentences.zh: 新立法包含促进房屋所有权和公共住房建设的条款。

sentences.en: And it also provided a bunch of money to clear blighted neighborhoods, or so-called sluMs.
sentences.zh: 它还提供了大量资金来清理破败的社区，也就是所谓的贫民窟。

sentences.en: If we don't clean out these slums, the central areas are going to rot.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不清理这些贫民窟，中心区域就会腐烂。

sentences.en: There are very few cases where genuine slums can be fixed up in any other way than by tearing them down.
sentences.zh: 除了拆除之外，很少有办法能真正修复真正的贫民窟。

sentences.en: That, of course, is Robert Moses, New York City's most prolific and problematic city planner.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是罗伯特·摩西，纽约市最多产也最具争议的城市规划师。

sentences.en: As diehard fans of the show will know, Robert Moses did more to reshape New York City in the 20th century
sentences.zh: 正如节目的铁杆粉丝所知，罗伯特·摩西在20世纪对纽约市的重塑，

sentences.en: than probably any other single person.
sentences.zh: 可能比任何其他个人都多。

sentences.en: After the American Housing Act was passed, Moses became head of New York City's Slum Clearance Committee.
sentences.zh: 《美国住房法》通过后，摩西成为了纽约市贫民窟清理委员会的负责人。

sentences.en: Part of what Moses wanted to do was replace these blighted buildings with public housing.
sentences.zh: 摩西想要做的一部分工作是用公共住房取代这些破败的建筑。

sentences.en: And in the post-war years, he did oversee the construction of a lot of public housing for low-income renters.
sentences.zh: 在战后岁月里，他确实监督建造了大量供低收入租户使用的公共住房。

sentences.en: But he and others in government also wanted housing for the middle class.
sentences.zh: 但他和政府中的其他人也希望为中产阶级提供住房。

sentences.en: In most other places, municipal governments sort of pursue like a two-pronged strategy for building new housing after World War II.
sentences.zh: 在大多数其他地方，市政当局在二战后采取了一种双管齐下的策略来建设新住房。
这位是安妮-玛丽·萨马蒂诺。

sentences.en: She's a professor of history at Oberlin College.
sentences.zh: 她是奥柏林学院的历史学教授。

sentences.en: On the one hand, there's housing projects for the very poor that are in the urban core.
sentences.zh: 一方面，城市核心区有为极度贫困人口提供的住房项目。

sentences.en: And then there's single-family, you know, sort of mortgage support for single-family homes.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，有针对单户住宅的抵押贷款支持。

sentences.en: New York's a little bit different because the mayor and other people in city government, they want to keep the middle class.
sentences.zh: 纽约有点不同，因为市长和市政府里的其他人想留住中产阶级。

sentences.en: And when they're saying this, they don't just mean the white middle class, but they mostly mean the white middle class living in New York City.
sentences.zh: 当他们这么说时，他们指的不仅仅是白人中产阶级，但他们主要指的确实是住在纽约市的白人中产阶级。

sentences.en: But it wasn't easy to find developers who wanted to get into the business of slum clearance in order to build homes for the middle class.
sentences.zh: 但要找到愿意为了给中产阶级盖房而从事贫民窟清理工作的开发商并不容易。

sentences.en: On the short list of groups willing to do the work were the unions and socialists.
sentences.zh: 愿意做这项工作的少数群体名单上，就有工会和社会主义者。

sentences.en: They'd already started building housing cooperatives in blighted neighborhoods and were anxious to build more.
sentences.zh: 他们已经开始在破败的社区建造合作住房，并渴望建造更多。

sentences.en: And the person most associated with this movement was our guy, Abraham Kazin.
sentences.zh: 而与这场运动联系最紧密的人就是我们的主角，亚伯拉罕·卡津。

sentences.en: Kazin and Moses worked quite closely together.
sentences.zh: 卡津和摩西合作得非常紧密。

sentences.en: And they realized that in a lot of ways they had overlapping visions for the future of the city, you know, that both of them wanted to replace slums with better housing.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到在很多方面，他们对城市未来的愿景是重叠的，你知道，他们都想用更好的住房取代贫民窟。

sentences.en: In 1951, Kazin created an organization dedicated to doing just that.
sentences.zh: 1951年，卡津成立了一个专门致力于此的组织。

sentences.en: It was called the United Housing Foundation or UHF.
sentences.zh: 它被称为联合住房基金会（UHF）。

sentences.en: And it's an alliance, basically, of existing cooperative projects, of unions and working class fraternal groups.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是现有合作社项目、工会和工人阶级兄弟会组织的联盟。

sentences.en: So, you know, they band together to create the UHF.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们联合起来创建了UHF。

sentences.en: And Kazin is like, you know, the leader.
I mean, he's got lieutenants, but he's the guy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他有副手，但他才是核心人物。

sentences.en: Then in 1955, New York State created a program called Mitchell-Lama.
sentences.zh: 然后在1955年，纽约州创建了一个名为“米切尔-拉马”（Mitchell-Lama）的项目。

sentences.en: It gave private developers like the UHF more incentive to build middle-class housing by offering them low interest rate mortgages and tax breaks.
sentences.zh: 它通过提供低利率抵押贷款和税收减免，给了像UHF这样的私人开发商更多建造中产阶级住房的动力。

sentences.en: For a wonky government program, Mitchell-Lama is still weirdly well-known in New York.
sentences.zh: 对于一个枯燥的政府项目来说，米切尔-拉马在纽约仍然出奇地出名。

sentences.en: And one of the many answers people might give to the question, where did you grow up?
sentences.zh: 它是人们回答“你在哪里长大？”这个问题时可能会给出的众多答案之一。

sentences.en: Like, I grew up in a brownstone.
sentences.zh: 比如，我在褐砂石建筑里长大。

sentences.en: I grew up in the projects.
I grew up in a Mitchell-Lama.
sentences.zh: 我在米切尔-拉马项目里长大。

sentences.en: If I may take us on a very quick digression to prove my point.
sentences.zh: 请允许我做一个非常简短的题外话来证明我的观点。

sentences.en: Here is Timothee Chalamet on Theo Vaughn's podcast back in 2024.
sentences.zh: 这是2024年提莫西·查拉梅在西奥·沃恩播客上的谈话。

sentences.en: I grew up in like a Mitchell-Lama.
sentences.zh: 我是在米切尔-拉马那种地方长大的。
是餐厅评级还是什么的？

sentences.en: At this point in the interview, Timothee does a pretty bad job of explaining what Mitchell-Lama is.
sentences.zh: 在采访的这一点上，提莫西在解释什么是米切尔-拉马方面做得相当糟糕。

sentences.en: But he gets one of the main things right.
It was meant to be housing for people of moderate income.
sentences.zh: 它本意是为中等收入人群提供的住房。
哦，该死的米切尔-拉马，兄弟。

sentences.en: Mitchell-Lama was launched in an era of big government liberalism.
sentences.zh: 米切尔-拉马诞生于大政府自由主义时代。

sentences.en: The state was subsidizing not just housing for the poor, but for people of middle income, like construction workers and teachers.
sentences.zh: 政府补贴的不仅是穷人的住房，还有中等收入人群，比如建筑工人和教师的住房。

sentences.en: In the Mitchell-Lama years, the program would finance over 100,000 units of affordable housing for the middle class.
sentences.zh: 在米切尔-拉马计划实施期间，该项目为中产阶级提供了超过10万套经济适用房。
